title: DJMax Technika Tune
subtitle: An arcade music game moves under the fingers
summary: DJMax Technika Tune is Pentavision's PlayStation Vita rhythm game, first released in South Korea and Hong Kong on 20 September 2012. body: DJMax Technika Tune is Pentavision's PlayStation Vita rhythm game, first released in South Korea and Hong Kong on 20 September 2012. It adapts the touch-driven Technika arcade series to the handheld, using the front screen and rear touchpad to turn musical patterns into gestures. Notes appear across the playfield and must be activated in time with the moving musical sequence. The player is doing more than following a list of button prompts. The arrangement of touches becomes part of the performance, connecting rhythm to where a hand needs to move next.

Beginner modes simplify the charts, allowing the player to become comfortable with the timing before longer, repeated and chained notes are introduced. More demanding arrangements ask for coordinated movement across the screen and touchpad, giving familiar songs another level of physical complexity. Repeated play makes a pattern recognisable, so the next gesture can be prepared rather than improvised at the last moment. The handheld's surfaces give the arcade idea a new scale: a large cabinet interaction is condensed into something held directly in the player's hands without losing its emphasis on touching the music's visual structure.

Producer Planetboom and designer XeoN led a release that also includes modes for listening to the soundtrack and watching its music videos. The North American edition contains sixty-seven tracks, giving the rhythm system a broad collection of charts to learn. Japan received the game in September 2012 and North America in December. Technika Tune belongs to the wider DJMax series but uses the Vita's particular hardware to establish its own play style. The result connects a specialised arcade tradition to a portable machine capable of making both sides of its body part of the input.
